subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, devices, and operators?
rationale: The source gap is real and the Gateway has relevant event primitives, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes security expectations and may add public CLI/config surface.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for a selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core mirror mode
options.body: Keep logs, sessions tailing, or a future approved activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid core cross-channel transcript mirroring.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for a selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main TUI/session history signal and this choice is primarily a TUI/session visibility product boundary decision.
